method.preprocessing: Mean, linear trend and solar harmonics 1-4 removed by least squares; the residual screen also removes the forcing year's harmonics 1-4 and the solar harmonics' sidebands one and two forcing years away (the first screen's basis).
method.spectrum: Welch, 768-record segments (2288 d), 384 overlap, linear detrend per segment; ratio to the AR(1) spectrum of the residual's lag-one correlation (clipped to (-0.98, 0.995)) scaled to its variance.
method.search: Periods 8-2200 d, 4% away from the solar day and its harmonics 2 and 3.
method.surrogates: Surrogates per series and window ({'main': 10000, 'compare': 10000, 'first half': 5000, 'second half': 5000, 'memory main': 5000, 'memory second half': 2000}): AR(1) at the residual's correlation and variance for the screens, the fitted two-timescale sum for "memory", each through the same regression, spectrum and fit; seed 20261108 (the memory null on its own stream).
method.within_series: Single-step max-statistic p-value: share of surrogate maxima at or above a peak's ratio (Westfall and Young 1993).
method.across_series: Holm (1979) step-down over the 234 series at 0.05, valid under any dependence (the regions nest and the fields share the weather); a peak is significant when its series passes Holm and its p-value times the number of series is at most the level. Benjamini and Hochberg (1995) given as the permissive reading.
method.memory_null: Two-timescale red noise: each residual's autocorrelation over lags 1-120 records fitted as the sum of a fast and a slow AR(1); surrogates of the sum through the same regression, spectrum and ratio give p-values under a null that holds the series' long memory.
method.lines: Known lines tested by fitted amplitude against the surrogates' amplitudes, Holm across series per line.
method.halves: Amplitude and phase at the line's frequency in each half (run time from the start of year 0); p_same_line is the chi-square (2 dof) test that the halves' complex amplitudes differ only by the fitted red noise at that frequency.
method.red_noise_reference: AR(1) red-noise spectrum: Gilman, Fuglister and Mitchell (1963).

inputs.digest_rule: SHA-256 of tas, pr (mm/day), ps, uas, vas, rst - rsut and czen as float32, in that order, as the first screen recorded them

evidence: Spectral tests of one model realization: ExoPlaSim T21 3-day regional means over the stated years, against AR(1) red noise fitted to each series, with the family-wise error controlled across frequencies by surrogate maxima and across the series by Holm. A significant peak is a departure from AR(1) noise in this run. The attribution tags are rules applied to computed facts (the forcing catalogue, the halves' phase test, the sunlight series); the written attribution lives with the climate README. The seas are 50 m mixed layers without currents, so the run's internal variability on long periods is a slab ocean's; nothing here is an observation of the Moon or a forecast.
reading_rule: Periods in days, from records 2.979 days apart. Amplitudes are half the peak-to-trough range of a fitted sinusoid in the field's units (tas K, pr mm/day, ps hPa, uas and vas m/s, incoming W/m2); phases are in degrees of y = A cos(2 pi t / period - phase), t in days from the start of model year 0 (file years of 357.5 days). Regions are latitude a:b N, longitude c:d E in the turned frame. p_series is the within-series max-statistic p-value against AR(1) surrogates (floor 1/(surrogates + 1)); series_holm is the series' Holm-adjusted p-value over all series; p_bonferroni is p_series times the number of series; significant means both at most 0.05. windows: "main" is the stated years, "compare" the first screen's years 10-28, the halves split the main window. forced_lines give each known line's significant series (Holm per line) and, for the strongest, the halves' amplitudes and phases with p_same_line, large when one line fits both halves; for a peak the search found, the frequency is fitted to the whole window, which favours one where the halves agree, so there p_same_line leans toward agreement and the halves' own ratios and p-values are the test of persistence. candidates settle the first screen's named features. persistence_of_main_peaks carries each significant peak of the main window into the halves with its attribution tag: forced (rule) when a line of the catalogue lies within half the record's resolution, p_same_line >= 0.01 and the sunlight of some region has a significant peak in the same bin; otherwise continuum (rule) when the two-timescale null explains it (p_memory_bonferroni > 0.05), internal (rule) when no line lies near and p_same_line < 0.01, undetermined otherwise. memory gives each series' fitted fast share, fast and slow lag-one correlations and misfit, and the slow component's e-folding in days.
